name: 29795-decodeheavy-30ba3b-dp8ep
hardware: 8x H100 80GB HBM3, all eight GPUs of one a3 node (--gres=gpu:8).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=8 with expert parallelism on, so ep_size = dp x tp = 8 and the 128 experts are split 16 to a rank. Eight engine cores in one process group, driven by the engine's internal load balancer.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=256, warmup the first 10% and cooldown the last 10%, bounded at 4096 requests with a 2400 s safety cap, static seed 29795.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn: 128 prompt tokens and 1024 output tokens per request, min == max == mean on both. EOS is ignored and max_tokens is pinned to 1024, so every request generates all 1024 tokens. The prompt is rendered and tokenized by the engine, so the prompt count it logs runs a few tokens above 128.
purpose: A long-form writing assistant generating 1024-token replies from short prompts for 256 concurrent users on eight GPUs.
launch:
# vLLM engine arguments for this item. Flat `key: value` only.

model: Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B

# With expert parallelism on at TP=1, ep_size = dp_size x tp_size = 8, so the 128 experts split 16
# to a rank and no expert is cut in half. `data-parallel-size-local` is left unset: it defaults to
# the global DP size, and all eight ranks are on this one node.
tensor-parallel-size: 1
data-parallel-size: 8
enable-expert-parallel: true

# Per engine core, so the declared 256 streams (~32 per rank) never approach the cap.
max-num-seqs: 1024

# This workload's worst case is 128 + 1024 = 1152 tokens; 2048 clears it with room for tokenizer
# drift in guidellm's synthetic prompts.
max-model-len: 2048

# Below the usual 0.95 on purpose: eight engine cores in one process group put communication
# buffers on each card OUTSIDE vLLM's own budget, and 0.95 leaves no room for them. KV is nowhere
# near binding either way.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
